case_title: Nagji Odha Vji Kumbhar & Anr. v. State of Gujarat
accused_victim_relationship: Prior enmity/dispute: land and right-of-way dispute; complainant party had obtained an injunction in a civil suit
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302 r/w s.34; IPC s.324 (r/w s.34)
evidence_type: Eyewitness (injured witnesses PW-3 and PW-4); medical (PW-2 and PW-10 injury evidence; post-mortem report)
aggravating_circumstances: Multiple stab wounds on the chest, a vital part, of both deceased; attack by seven to eight armed persons on unarmed victims
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under s.302 IPC; life imprisonment; no separate punishment under s.324
high_court_outcome: Appeal (Criminal Appeal No. 234 of 1990) dismissed on 24.10.2008; conviction under ss.302 and 324 maintained
offence_finally_established: IPC s.302 r/w s.34 (murder of two persons); IPC s.324 conviction maintained
neutral_facts: On the night of 1 July 1987, at about midnight in a village, a group of men confronted two victims over a long-running dispute about a right of way over land. The accused group was said to be armed: one man carried a spear, another an axe, and others sticks. Both victims were stabbed and struck and died at the spot. Two men present, including the complainant, were injured and were examined by a doctor, whose evidence recorded their wounds. The complainant's statement formed the basis of the first information report, lodged at 7 AM the next morning. Post-mortem examination of the two victims recorded stab wounds to the chest, including wounds to the lungs, consistent with the oral evidence that both had received stab wounds. The accused, arrested later in July, also had injuries examined by the same doctor. Their account was that the victims' side, nine in number, had attacked them, and the investigating officer testified that one accused was lying bleeding at the scene. The injured eyewitnesses described the attackers as armed with spears and other weapons. The accused's first account, lodged as a cross-complaint, stated that the victims were not armed.
physical_harm: Death of two victims from stab wounds to the chest (lungs, vessels and trachea cut); injuries to both accused, including head wounds, cut and bone-deep wounds and fractures
number_of_offences: 2 charged; 2 finally upheld (s.302 and s.324; no separate sentence under s.324)
premeditation_planning: Not expressly found; the court rejected the spur-of-the-moment plea because of multiple wounds on vital parts
motive: alleged: dispute over right of way to the deceased (the court did not decide motive)
key_evidence_accepted: Eyewitness testimony of injured witnesses PW-3 and PW-4 (attack by armed appellants); PW-2 and PW-10 injury evidence; post-mortem report corroborating stab wounds
witness_credibility: Injured eyewitnesses PW-3 and PW-4 accepted as reliable; their presence not seriously disputed; medical report corroborates their account. The Investigating Officer's account that one accused lay bleeding was held not to merit consideration
custody_duration: Defence submitted more than 11 years of actual imprisonment; the appellants were arrested on 17 July 1987
trial_duration: offence: 1 July 1987; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 24.10.2008; Supreme Court: 23 April 2019
legal_representation: Accused: Ravi Prakash Mehrotra, Ankit Agarwal, Ms. Deepti R. Mehrotra (Advocates). State of Gujarat: Ms. Jesal Wahi (for Ms. Hemantika Wahi), Advocate
investigation_status: FIR registered 2 July 1987; accused arrested 17 July 1987; investigation completed and trial conducted; cross-case FIR under separate trial
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted under s.302, life imprisonment. High Court: conviction maintained on 24.10.2008 (Criminal Appeal No. 234 of 1990). Supreme Court: appeal dismissed
prosecution_argument: Relied on injured eyewitness statements (PW-3, PW-4) and medical evidence (PW-2, PW-10, post-mortem) to establish armed attack by the accused; the judgment records no separate State submissions
defence_argument: Deceased side were aggressors; accused injured while protecting their land, so acted in private defence; alternatively, the act was on the spur of the moment without pre-meditation, so conviction should be under s.304 Part II; relied on Jangir Singh
legal_principle_applied: Private defence unavailable where the victims were unarmed; the right cannot justify harm beyond what is necessary; a plea of spur-of-the-moment killing fails where multiple wounds are inflicted on vital parts
precedent_relied_upon: Jangir Singh v. State of Punjab, 2018 (15) SCALE 88 (Criminal Appeal No. 2499 of 2009) – distinguished
sentencing_rationale: Not applicable (the court upheld the trial sentence without separate sentencing reasoning)
judicial_aggravating_factors: Multiple injuries on vital parts (chest) of the deceased
